method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 53 spans 24th-27th St, sheet 59 spans 27th-30th, so 27th is the only shared street; sheet 53 prints '27TH 59 ST.' in its bottom band and sheet 59 prints '27TH ST.' with '53' in its top band. The avenue-frontage runs change hundred-block exactly across it: the block north of the street (sheet 53) carries 2601/2603/2605...2627 and 2602/2604/2606...2628, i.e. the 26th-27th segment; the block south of it (sheet 59) carries 2701/2703/2705...2731 and 2702/2704/2706...2732, the 27th-28th segment. One street south on sheet 59 the change is 27xx->28xx at 28th St (2801/2803, 2802/2804 beyond it, north faces 1247.5 / south 1490); one street north on sheet 53 the change is 25xx->26xx at 26th St (2518/2520 above it, 2601/2602 below; faces 2458/2692). The street-frontage numbers 1813/1815/1817/1819/1821/1823 and 1814-1824 are printed on BOTH sheets against this corridor - the same segment seen from its two sides, which is what identifies it as one street rather than two.
note: Detection candidates (53: 3276/2113/950; 59: 660/1819/2978) are mid-block lines. Sheet 59 shows both faces of the corridor, at native y 104 and 345 (width 241 px = the printed 80'; the sheet's Scale of Feet bar gives 3.00 px/ft), so its centre is 224.5. Sheet 53 shows only the north face, at native y 3596; the far face would fall at ~3837, essentially at the paper edge (3850), so its centre is 3596 + 120.5 = 3716.5.
